newsitem.title: USA: Indiana wheat rated 66 pct good to excellent.
newsitem.headline: Indiana wheat rated 66 pct good to excellent.

text.p: Indiana's winter wheat was rated 14 percent excellent and 52 percent good during the week ended Sunday, according to Indiana's Agricultural Statistics Service.

That is a decline from 70 percent in the good-to-excellent category a week ago. The state's service said the wheat condition ratings during the next few weeks will indicate whether the crop was damaged by sub-freezing temperatures during the past week.
Thirteen percent of the wheat crop was jointed, compared with three percent a year ago and the five-year average of nine percent.
Corn planting was under way in scaattered fields around the state with one percent in the ground as of Sunday, ahead of the zero percent pace of a year ago and average.
Pasture conditions were five percent excellent, 46 percent good, 35 percent fair, 10 percent poor and four percent very poor.
Topsoil moisture was three percent short, 68 percent adequate and 29 percent surplus.
